parts.title: The Big Idea
parts.text: Vivian, Ahmed and Luca ran a bike-repair business from Luca's garage, and it was growing. Vivian dreamed of buying a van so they could fix bikes at neighborhood parks. She wrote a formal **proposal** for a credit union's youth loan program, explaining exactly how the money would be spent. The loan officer asked for **collateral**, something valuable the credit union could claim if the loan went unpaid, so the partners pledged their tools and the van itself.

parts.title: Counting Costs
parts.text: Ahmed, the **shrewd** one, studied their budget and spotted a problem. Every month, the **overhead**, meaning rent for the garage, insurance and electricity, swallowed a third of their income. "We must **scrimp** on supplies until the loan arrives," he said. He also warned that one terrible season could leave them **bankrupt**, unable to pay what they owed.

parts.title: Growing Pains
parts.text: To **entice** new customers, the team offered free tire checks at the park. Their **clientele**, once mostly neighbors, grew to include a school team and a delivery club. A rival shop owner suggested they **merge** the two businesses, and after long talks they signed an **equitable** agreement that split the work and the profits fairly. The loan officer also urged them to **diversify** by selling helmets and bells, so a slow season could not sink them. Within a year, each partner received a **dividend**, a share of the profits, for the first time.

parts.title: Reflections
parts.text: On the last day of school, Vivian looked at the van, painted in bright green, and laughed at how small the idea had once seemed. The business had taught her that good planning is only part of success; the rest is patience, honest teamwork and the willingness to keep learning. Ahmed and Luca already had plans for next summer.

definitions.meaning1: A formal plan or suggestion put forward for others to consider. Example: Her proposal for a school garden won the principal's approval.
definitions.meaning2: A request to marry someone. Example: His proposal took place at sunrise on the beach.

definitions.meaning1: Clever at judging situations, especially in practical or money matters. Example: A shrewd shopper, she waited for the sale before buying the coat.
definitions.studentChallenge: The ___ negotiator got a lower price without sounding rude.

definitions.meaning1: Property or valuables pledged to a lender to guarantee a loan will be repaid. Example: He used his car as collateral for the loan.
definitions.meaning2: Secondary or side, as in an unintended side effect. Example: The storm caused collateral damage to nearby fences.
definitions.studentChallenge: The bank would not lend the money without ___ to protect itself.

definitions.meaning1: A share of a company's profits paid to its owners or investors. Example: The company paid a dividend of two dollars per share.
definitions.meaning2: A benefit gained from effort or investment. Example: Years of daily practice paid dividends when she won the recital.
definitions.studentChallenge: Each owner received a small ___ after the profitable year.

definitions.meaning1: To attract by offering something appealing. Example: The bakery used free samples to entice customers inside.

definitions.meaning1: The customers or clients of a business, thought of as a group. Example: The salon's clientele included both teenagers and retirees.
definitions.studentChallenge: The restaurant's loyal ___ returned every Friday for the same dish.

definitions.meaning1: Unable to pay debts, and legally declared so. Example: The toy company went bankrupt after its warehouse flooded.
definitions.meaning2: Completely lacking in a quality. Example: The speech was bankrupt of fresh ideas.
definitions.studentChallenge: After years of losses, the shop went ___ and closed its doors.

definitions.meaning1: Fair and impartial; treating everyone equally. Example: The twins worked out an equitable way to share the last cookie.
definitions.studentChallenge: The coach made the schedule ___ so every player got time on the field.

definitions.meaning1: To combine into one. Example: The two schools will merge into a single campus next year.
definitions.meaning2: To blend gradually so that differences disappear. Example: At sunset, the colors seemed to merge across the sky.
definitions.studentChallenge: Two small rivers ___ here to form one large river.

definitions.meaning1: To spend very little money, usually in order to save. Example: The family had to scrimp on groceries to pay the rent.
definitions.studentChallenge: She learned to ___ and save every dollar for college.

definitions.meaning1: The regular costs of running a business, such as rent and utilities. Example: High overhead made it hard for the bakery to turn a profit.
definitions.meaning2: Located above your head. Example: An overhead light flickered in the hallway.
definitions.studentChallenge: The shop owner cut ___ by switching to cheaper electricity.

definitions.meaning1: To add variety, especially by expanding into new areas to reduce risk. Example: The farm began to diversify by growing berries as well as corn.
definitions.studentChallenge: Smart investors ___ so that one bad stock will not ruin them.
